cases.question: Trace Gson.fromJson across its String, Reader, JsonReader and JsonElement entry points in this checkout. Identify every declared overload and its target-type routing, including what a Class argument selects for JsonReader. Explain Java-null inputs versus JsonNull, parsing and full-consumption boundaries (including a null adapter result), reader strictness selection and restoration timing, adapter lookup/read/result validation, and exception behavior by phase. Distinguish an EOFException from the initial peek from later EOF and a peek returning END_DOCUMENT; include exception causes, AssertionError handling and exceptions that are not caught. Assume valid non-null target-type arguments and valid non-null Reader/JsonReader objects, but do not assume custom adapters return the requested type, consume exactly one value, or succeed. Stay at these entry-point and adapter boundaries; do not enumerate adapter factories or reflection internals, or execute the project. Provide one representative contiguous source quote per finding and explain the complete behavior, synthesizing other relevant source ranges when needed. Evidence boundary: read repository files with ordinary source tools; do not read parent-directory case catalogs, rubrics, controls, other trial artifacts, or any other private experiment files. In the Columbus condition only, the explicitly supplied frozen runtime skill/references and saved graph are also allowed; baseline must not inspect them.

findings.description: Enumerate the declared overload shapes, Class/Type-to-TypeToken delegation and return casts, String and tree wrappers, and the common JsonReader entry point. Explain how Class arguments work without a declared JsonReader/Class overload. Use the Reader/TypeToken handoff as the representative citation.

Explain the Java-null String and Java-null tree shortcuts, where they occur relative to wrapping/delegation, and how JsonNull differs. Keep the stated valid-target assumption. Use the tree-input shortcut as the representative citation.

Compare String/Reader completion checking with direct JsonReader and tree entry points. Include null-result behavior, trailing-token detection, and malformed versus other I/O failures during the completion check. Use the completion-check implementation as the representative citation.

Explain new-reader defaults, explicit Gson strictness versus an existing reader's LEGACY_STRICT/LENIENT/STRICT setting, and restoration on success or failure, including its timing relative to the completion check. Use the core JsonReader strictness-selection branch as the representative citation.

Explain the order of initial peek, adapter lookup, reading and result validation; null handling, primitive wrapping, assignability versus exact/generic-content checks, and mismatch exceptions. Use the core adapter-read and result-check sequence as the representative citation.

Explain initial-peek EOFException versus later EOF and END_DOCUMENT, IllegalStateException and I/O translation, AssertionError version/cause handling, and the limits of the catches. Distinguish this parse phase from completion-check I/O handling. Use the core catch/finally block as the representative citation.
